when: you died in the last minute and your lane opponent has more CS than you
asks: I got dived and now the wave's frozen
he's holding the wave on me, what do I do
I can't walk up to farm
how do I get back in lane after dying
wave is stuck on his side
say: Stand back and soak experience until the wave pushes to you, or ask your jungler to break it if he's on your side.
more: One dive costs a wave. The second dive is what ends the lane, and it comes when you walk up low to fight for minions.
A wave held on his side has to tip over eventually. Experience alone keeps you a level or so behind instead of out of the game.
If your jungler comes, the two of you push it into his tower and the lane resets to normal.
check: Where is the wave sitting, how many of his minions are stacked, and where was their jungler last seen?
breaks: Wrong if he has left lane to roam: then walk up, shove the wave hard and take the plate before he returns.
basis: pro:After a dive, the second dive is the danger

when: your top or bot laner died under their own tower in the last minute
asks: my top just got dived, do I go there
should I help the lane that just died
they dove bot, where do I go now
do I cover top or keep farming
my laner keeps getting dived
say: Go stand behind that tower for the next big wave so the second dive fails, or take the far objective if three of them show there.
more: A team that dived once will come back on the next stacked wave, because the laner returns weaker and the wave is still theirs.
You don't need a kill. Being seen there lets your laner collect the wave, and that is what keeps him in the game.
If they commit three again anyway, nothing is defending the other side of the map, so the trade is open.
check: Is a big wave about to hit that tower, and is their jungler unaccounted for?
breaks: Wrong if the wave is small or pushing away from your laner: there is nothing to dive with, so farm or gank elsewhere.
basis: pro:Cover the second dive, not the first

when: you are level 6 and your lane opponent is level 5
asks: I hit six first, what do I do with it
I'm a level up top, how do I use it
should I all in or hold the wave
he's still five and I'm six
do I shove or freeze with a level lead
say: Hold the wave on your side and stand between him and it while you're a level up, or shove for plates if their jungler shows top.
more: An ultimate he doesn't have yet means he can't walk up. Every wave he watches die widens the gap without you risking anything.
Killing him is a bonus. Making him choose between minions and his health is the real win, and it often burns his Flash.
When he catches up in level the threat is gone, so use the minute you have.
check: Is the wave on your half of the lane, and do you know where their jungler is?
breaks: Wrong if the wave is already under his tower: you can't zone there, so crash it, recall and come back with the item.
basis: pro:A level lead holds the wave

when: it is between 7:00 and 8:00 and you have more CS and levels than your lane opponent
asks: I'm winning top, grubs are about to spawn
should I leave lane for grubs
do I help my jungler at grubs or keep farming
I'm ahead top what do I do at eight minutes
grubs or plates
say: Shove the wave under his tower just before 8:00 and walk to grubs first, or stay on plates if your jungler's on the other side.
more: A top laner stuck under his own tower can't come to the pit, so your jungler takes grubs with you standing guard.
Grubs don't come back. A lead in top lane is the cheapest way to make that one window free.
If your jungler isn't coming, the same shoved wave still pays you in plates.
check: Is your wave actually crashed into his tower, and has your jungler pinged the pit?
breaks: Wrong if he has Teleport and you don't and the wave is in the middle: he takes your tower while you're at the pit.
basis: pro:A winning top lane makes grubs free

when: the enemy top laner and mid laner are both magic damage champions
asks: what do I build first top
their top and mid are both AP
do I buy magic resist early
what item into this lane
they have two mages in solo lanes
say: Buy magic resist first; it holds lane now and both side lanes later, or keep your normal first item if their jungler's the fed one.
more: After lanes break up you meet either their top or their mid in a side lane. One resist item answers both of them.
With it you can stand in a trade he expects to win, so he loses the push and you get plates.
It also lets one of your team walk forward first at the early objective fights.
check: Who on their team is actually doing the damage right now, and what did your lane opponent buy?
breaks: Wrong if their attack damage jungler or carry is the one ahead: armor or health first, resist second.
basis: pro:One resist item answers two solo laners

when: your health is below a third and you are level 5 or lower
asks: I'm low but there's a wave coming
should I back or stay for the cannon
do I recall now
I'm low mid, can I stay
is it worth staying for this wave
say: Recall now even if it costs the wave, or stay only under your tower with Flash up and their support in sight.
more: A low mid laner before level 6 is the easiest target on the map. Their support or jungler can reach you from either side.
A wave is a small loss. A death gives him the wave, a kill and a lead that decides the next river fight.
Buy potions on that recall so the next bit of poke doesn't send you home again.
check: Can you see their support and jungler on the map, and is your Flash up?
breaks: Wrong if you have Teleport and the wave is about to crash into his tower: push it in first, then recall.
basis: pro:Do not stay low for one more wave

when: before 3:00 and the enemy support is an engage or tank champion
asks: their support keeps walking at me
can I trade level one
I'm a squishy support, where do I stand
he's standing in the brush
how do I not die level one
say: Stay behind your minions and off the walls until level two, or give the first push and poke only when he steps back.
more: Engage supports are strongest in the first two minutes, when you have one ability and no way out.
A level-one death gives their carry gold and brings their jungler down for a second kill on the next wave.
Once you have two abilities and they've used their engage, the lane turns back toward you.
check: Is he standing in a brush or near a wall, and does he still have Flash?
breaks: Wrong if their support has already used Flash and missed: step up and poke freely for the next few waves.
basis: pro:Respect the level-one engage

when: your bot lane got a kill before 3:00
asks: bot got first blood, do I go there
should I gank bot after they got a kill
bot lane is winning, do I help
do I finish my clear or go bot
say: Go bot again right away; whoever died has to walk up to that wave with no Flash, or finish your clear if they hug tower.
more: The lane that just died comes back behind and must still collect the wave, usually without summoner spells.
A second kill this early puts your carry an item ahead and makes the first dragon free.
It costs you camps, so only pay that price for a lane that is already winning.
check: Did the enemy use Flash when they died, and is the wave on your side or in the middle?
breaks: Wrong if the wave is under their tower and they're playing back: take your camps and come back on the next push.
basis: pro:Follow an early kill with the jungler

when: an enemy laner got a kill on your laner in the last 20 seconds
asks: my laner just died, do I go there
he just killed my mid, can I kill him
should I gank the lane that's losing
the guy who got the kill is still in lane
say: Gank that lane now; the killer is often low, pushed up and without Flash, or just hold the wave if he's recalled.
more: Winning a fight costs health and summoner spells. For half a minute the winner is weaker than he looks.
Even without the kill, your being there saves the wave for your laner when he walks back.
A shutdown this early pays for the camps you leave.
check: How low is the killer, did he use Flash, and is he still in lane?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler was part of the kill and is still there: you'd be walking into two, so farm the far side.
basis: pro:Gank the lane that just won

when: you are level 3 to 5 and the laner you want to gank has Flash
asks: he still has flash, is it worth ganking
do I gank even if he just flashes
I can't kill him, he'll flash away
should I gank mid or keep farming
say: Gank once to take his Flash, then come back after your next camps for the kill, or skip it if the wave's under his tower.
more: The first step in killing a laner is removing Flash. The second visit, while it's still down, is the one that pays.
Tell your laner it's gone. He can play forward for a few minutes knowing the other player can't escape.
Plan your clear so it ends beside that lane again, or the window passes.
check: Is the wave far enough from his tower to force Flash, and can your laner follow up?
breaks: Wrong if another lane already has no Flash: go there first, that kill is available now.
basis: pro:First gank takes Flash, second takes the kill

when: an enemy laner has died at least twice and is behind in level
asks: should I keep ganking the same lane
I already killed top twice, go again?
do I camp the lane that's losing
is it worth going back to the same guy
say: Keep going back to the lane you already broke; he can't hold a wave now, or switch if he's stacking armor under tower.
more: A laner two deaths down can't trade, so the wave sits in a long lane and he has to walk into it.
Each visit also grows your own laner, and a fed side laner pulls their whole team later.
The enemy jungler has to come and help. If he shows there, the other half of the map is yours.
check: Is that lane's wave on your side, and did their jungler show there recently?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler is waiting there or the target has stopped leaving tower: take the objective on the other side.
basis: pro:Go back to the lane that is already broken

asks: my laners stacked a huge wave, do I come
big wave bot, should I dive
is it worth going to the big wave
they're pinging me to dive with the wave
say: A big wave crashing into their tower is a dive or a denied wave, so go there first, or cover mid if your mid's low.
more: Stacked minions tank the tower and hide your approach. That is the safest dive you'll get.
Even with no kill, standing there with your laners makes the defender miss the whole wave.
The cost is whatever happens on the other side while three of you are in one lane.
check: How big is the wave, how many defenders are there, and where is their jungler?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler and mid are both missing: they can be waiting behind that tower, so ward first or leave it.
basis: pro:Follow the stacked wave

when: before 5:00 and your bot lane has less CS than theirs
asks: bot's getting pushed in, do I go
should I hover bot early
they're going to dive my bot lane
where do I path if bot's losing
say: On their first big crash, wait behind your bot tower instead of ganking elsewhere, or take the far crab if their jungler's top.
more: The first large wave under a losing bot tower is where early dives happen. One jungler standing there stops it.
If they dive anyway you get a counter-gank with tower shots on your side, which is the best fight you'll find early.
If nobody comes, you lost a little time and your carry kept the wave.
check: Is a large wave about to hit your bot tower, and has their jungler been seen?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler just showed on the top side: nobody can dive, so use the time to gank or farm.
basis: pro:Hover the first crash

when: your team took a dragon or grubs with no fight in the last 30 seconds
asks: nobody contested dragon, where are they
we got drake for free, now what
why did they just give us grubs
they didn't even show at dragon
say: If nobody contested, they went somewhere; hug your tower for the next half minute, or shove and leave if you see four of them.
more: A team that gives an objective for free is often already walking to a lane with three or four players.
The usual target is whoever has no Flash or hasn't reached level 6 yet.
Once they show on the map, everyone else on your team can push without fear.
check: How many enemies are visible on the map right now, and is your Flash up?
breaks: Wrong if all five are showing in their lanes: then they simply gave it, so keep farming normally.
basis: pro:A free objective means they went somewhere else

when: you just recalled and it is before 10:00
asks: should I roam mid as support
do I go straight back to lane
can I gank mid on my way back
when do I roam as support
I just backed, where do I go
say: Walk back through mid and threaten their mid laner on the way, or go straight bot if your carry's alone under tower.
more: You're passing mid anyway. A support appearing there with fresh items often takes a Flash for a few seconds of walking.
A Flash burned mid sets up your jungler's next gank and the first river fight.
Keep it short. If nothing happens in a few seconds, keep walking to lane.
check: Is their mid laner pushed past the middle of the lane, and is your carry safe?
breaks: Wrong if your carry is being zoned from a big wave: he loses more than mid gains, so go straight to lane.
basis: pro:Return to lane through mid

asks: their support left lane, do I follow
enemy support is roaming mid
should I follow the roam
their support's missing, what do I do
say: Follow right away or not at all: go at once if your mid's low, or shove the wave with your carry and ping mid.
more: Arriving a few seconds late is the worst result. Your mid is already dead and your carry was left alone for nothing.
Shoving instead makes their roam cost them a wave and plate damage, and your ping may save the Flash.
Decide in the first second he walks out of sight, not when the fight starts.
check: How low is your mid laner, and how far ahead of you is their support?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler is also missing near your lane: don't leave your carry and don't push, just hold near tower.
basis: pro:A late follow is the worst follow

when: the enemy jungler got a kill or assist on the top side in the last 20 seconds
asks: where do I ward right now
their jungler's top, what do I do bot
when is it safe to ward deep
should I go ward their jungle
say: He's top, so ward the entrances to their bottom jungle now, or put it on dragon if it spawns within a minute.
more: Deep wards are only safe when you know where their jungler is. A kill on the far side tells you exactly that.
Those wards show his next walk toward your lane and where he'll be before the dragon.
A team with their jungle lit can catch him on his own camps later.
check: Is your bot wave pushed enough to leave, and how many enemy laners are missing?
breaks: Wrong if their mid laner is missing too: he may be walking down, so ward the river and come back.
basis: pro:Ward the side their jungler just left

when: an objective spawns within a minute
asks: who checks the brush
do I walk into the river first
should I ward the pit myself
is it safe to go in there
nobody's warding, do I do it
say: Let your tank or support walk into the dark brush first, or throw an ability in to check it if you have to go alone.
more: Carries dying in a brush before the fight is the most common way a team with the lead loses an objective.
Your death there isn't one kill. It's the objective, because your team has no damage left to take or contest it.
Arrive a few seconds behind the front line and you lose nothing.
check: Who on your team is ahead of you, and how many enemies are showing on the map?
breaks: Wrong if all five enemies are visible elsewhere: then walk in and place the ward yourself.
basis: pro:Carries do not face-check

when: an objective spawns within a minute
asks: do I face check as support
should I go in first to ward
I keep dying warding
who goes into the brush first
how do I ward before dragon
say: You check the brush for your team, but only with damage right behind you, or ward from range if you're on your own.
more: A tanky support can take the first hit, and when your carries are a step behind, the ambush becomes your fight.
Checking alone just gives a kill and leaves your team without its engage for the objective.
Go early, while they are still walking over, not when the monster is already up.
check: Are your damage dealers within a second or two of you, and is your Flash up?
breaks: Wrong if you are behind and they have burst: don't check at all, give the brush and ward the path your team will use.
basis: pro:The tank checks, but never alone

when: Baron or Elder is alive
asks: are they doing baron
can they sneak baron right now
do we need to check the pit
is it safe to keep pushing
should we face check baron
say: If their fastest objective damage shows in a side lane, it isn't melting; use that time to ward, or group now if he's missing.
more: Most teams have one or two champions who make a quick Baron possible. Without them it's slow and loud.
Seeing those players elsewhere buys you the time to clear a wave or walk a ward in safely.
When they disappear together with the jungler, treat it as started.
check: Which of their champions kills big monsters fastest, and can you see him and their jungler?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler and carry are both missing: don't finish the wave, walk to the pit with your team.
basis: pro:Seeing their damage dealer rules out the rush

when: between 8:00 and 9:30 and grubs are alive
asks: they have more people at grubs
can I contest grubs outnumbered
we're late to grubs, what now
should I try to steal a grub
say: Don't walk in outnumbered; wait until one of them leaves for a wave and take one grub, or start dragon if nobody leaves.
more: Laners can't stay at the pit for long, because their waves are dying. The numbers usually change within seconds.
One grub taken away is a fair result for the side that arrived second, and it costs you nothing.
If all of them stay, they're paying for it in waves and the dragon is yours.
check: How many of them are at the pit, and is one already walking back to lane?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler has Smite ready and is standing on the grub: you get nothing, so trade for dragon at once.
basis: pro:Take one grub when their numbers leave

when: between 8:00 and 10:00 and grubs are alive
asks: they're coming while I do grubs
do I finish the last grub
should I smite this grub or wait
I have two grubs, do I stay for the third
say: Take what you can Smite and let the last one reset until Smite's back, or leave with two if their laners arrive.
more: A grub fought over without Smite is a coin flip you don't need. Two in hand already makes it a good trip.
Backing off resets the fight on your terms and lets your own laners catch up.
Waiting around loses waves in the nearby lane, so set a short limit.
check: Is your Smite up, where is their jungler, and are your laners on the way?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler is dead or showing bot: there's nobody to steal it, so finish all three.
basis: pro:Do not flip the last grub

when: a dragon is alive and it is before 14:00
asks: can I solo dragon
should I start drake alone
I'm a tank jungler, do I do dragon
dragon's up, nobody's coming
say: A tank takes dragon slowly, so ping bot to shove and come help, or gank instead if nobody can leave lane.
more: A slow take alone gives their mid and jungler time to walk over, and you're low when they arrive.
With your bot lane hitting it, the dragon dies before they can react and the lane loses very little.
If your bot lane can't move, that same time spent on a gank is worth more.
check: Is your bot wave pushed, and where were their jungler and mid last seen?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler just died or showed top: then start it alone, nobody is coming to stop you.
basis: pro:A slow dragon needs a second body

when: between 7:00 and 8:00, a dragon is alive and nobody has died in the last 30 seconds
asks: the dragon fight fizzled, do I restart it
everyone backed off drake, now what
do I stay for dragon or go grubs
should I recall before grubs
say: Leave the dragon, recall and be at grubs for 8:00, or restart it only if their jungler recalled before you did.
more: After a drawn skirmish everyone is low. Restarting a monster in that state hands the next spawn to the team that recalled.
Grubs are one window. Arriving healthy with gold spent matters more than the dragon you left.
The dragon will still be there, and you return with an item.
check: How low are you, how much gold are you holding, and did their jungler recall?
breaks: Wrong if grubs are already dead or this dragon would be their third: then stay and finish it.
basis: pro:After a drawn skirmish, play the next spawn

when: a dragon or Baron is alive and your team is behind in kills and towers
asks: can I steal it
should I go in for the smite
they're doing baron, do I flip it
is it worth trying to steal dragon
say: Go for the steal only on soul, Baron or Elder and with a way out; otherwise take their camps or a tower.
more: A failed steal on an ordinary dragon costs your life and your Smite at the next one too.
On the objectives that end games the maths changes: your death is cheap against what it prevents.
Come over a wall they aren't watching, and only when the monster is nearly dead.
check: Is this the one that gives soul, Baron or Elder, and can you get out after Smiting?
breaks: Wrong if your team is close enough to fight with you: then it's a team fight, not a solo steal.
basis: pro:Steal attempts are for the objectives that end games

when: an objective spawns within 90 seconds
asks: we have a poke comp, how do we take dragon
when do I go to the objective
we got there late, do we still go
should we walk into the river
say: Your comp has to be there first, so recall early and set up a minute ahead, or give it if they already hold the river.
more: Poke and zone abilities are strong at holding ground and poor at taking it back.
Walking into a river they already control means your damage starts after their engage lands.
If you're late, the same wave clear gets you a tower on the other side.
check: Which team has players in the river now, and are your side waves pushed?
breaks: Wrong if their engage champion is dead or showing far away: then walk in late, nothing can start on you.
basis: pro:Zone comps arrive first or not at all

when: the enemy bot carry has at least two more kills and one more finished item than yours
asks: their adc is fed, do we fight
can we contest with their carry that strong
how do we play against a fed adc
do we give dragon
say: Don't fight where their fed carry is; contest only when he shows in another lane, or trade for towers and camps.
more: One carry far ahead decides any even fight he stands in. Take the fights he isn't standing in.
Watch the map for him. When he shows in a side lane, the objective or the pick on the other side is on.
This buys time for your own items without giving shutdown gold away.
check: Where is their carry showing right now, and how many items does yours have?
breaks: Wrong if this dragon gives them soul: you have to fight it, so aim everything at him first.
basis: pro:Fight where the fed carry is not

when: no objective spawns within 90 seconds and you have Teleport
asks: should I group or stay in side lane
my team wants me to group
when do I leave my lane
do I keep farming side
say: Stay in the side lane and take waves until about a minute before the spawn, or leave sooner if you have no Teleport.
more: Standing with four others when nothing is up just splits one wave five ways. Side waves are levels and items.
The top laner who kept farming arrives at the objective a level ahead of the one who grouped early.
Your pushed wave also holds one of them in that lane when the fight starts.
check: When does the next objective spawn, and how many enemies can you see?
breaks: Wrong if four enemies are missing and you're past the river: back off now, they are coming for you.
basis: pro:Grouping early costs the side laner

when: you do not have Teleport and the outer towers are down
asks: which lane do I go to
can I side lane as a mage
should I go top or bot after laning
where do I farm now
say: Without Teleport, take the side lane nearest the next objective and stay on your half, or swap with whoever has it.
more: A mage on the far side with no Teleport is either caught or missing from the fight. Both cost the objective.
On the near side you can farm until the last moment and still walk there.
Staying on your half makes them send two or three deep to reach you, which opens the map for your team.
check: Which objective spawns next, and where is the wave in that side lane?
breaks: Wrong if your team needs your wave clear in mid to stop a siege: stay mid and let the side wave come to you.
basis: pro:No Teleport, no far side lane

when: you are at least two levels ahead of your lane opponent
asks: they keep sending three people to me
I'm fed in side lane, what now
should I keep split pushing
they're all coming top
say: If three come for you, ping it and back off slowly while your team takes something, or leave early if nothing's up there.
more: Pulling three is the job. Your team has a short window to take a tower, a dragon or their camps at four against two.
Use the time they spend walking to you, and don't give them a quick kill.
If your team can't take anything, the push has no purpose and you're only risking your shutdown.
check: How many are walking to you, and is there an objective or tower your team can reach?
breaks: Wrong if your team is dead or in base: there is nothing to trade, so stop at the river and farm safely.
basis: pro:Pulling three is the split pusher's job

when: the enemy team has Nocturne and he is level 6 or higher
asks: can I side lane against Nocturne
is it safe to split
Nocturne keeps ulting me
how do I play side lane into Nocturne
say: Against Nocturne, don't push alone past the river; stay near a teammate, or go deep right after he uses Paranoia elsewhere.
more: Paranoia cuts your vision and takes away what your allies see, then he launches at you, so a ward doesn't save a lone side laner.
His kill or assist somewhere else tells you it's just been used. That's your window to take the deep wave.
It is much worse without Flash, so count that too.
check: Where did Nocturne last show, did he just use his ultimate, and is your Flash up?
breaks: Wrong if he is dead or you can see him on the far side: push as deep as the wave lets you.
basis: pro:A vision-cutting dive punishes the lone side laner

when: the enemy team has Swain
asks: how do we fight Swain
Swain just walks into us
what do I do when Swain ults
he's healing off all of us
say: Back out of range while Demonic Ascension is running and return when it ends, or burst him first if he's walked in alone.
more: His ultimate drains everyone near him. The more of you stand in it, the longer he lives.
Stepping away for those seconds wastes his main fight tool, and then he's a slow target in the middle of you.
He needs his team hitting you while you're slowed. Alone, he's just buying time.
check: Has he transformed yet, and is the rest of his team close enough to follow?
breaks: Wrong if your team has heavy burst and he has no help: kill him at once rather than backing off.
basis: pro:Walk out of the drain, then fight

when: the enemy team has Poppy
asks: Poppy keeps stopping my dash
how do I engage into Poppy
I can't get on their carry with Poppy there
what do I do about Poppy W
say: Bait out Steadfast Presence before you dash in, or go on someone standing well away from her.
more: That ability stops dashes around her. If your engage is a dash, it ends where she stands.
Walk at them, let her press it, step back and go again a few seconds later.
She also has Keeper's Verdict to knock someone far away, so go in together, not one at a time.
check: Is Poppy standing next to the target, and has she used the ability in the last few seconds?
breaks: Wrong if your way in is not a dash: ignore it and engage normally.
basis: pro:Wait out the anti-dash

when: you have Cleanse
asks: where do I stand in fights as adc
can I play forward with cleanse
they always engage on me
how do I bait their engage
say: With Cleanse up you can stand a step forward to draw their engage and fall back to your team, or play far back when it's down.
more: Their engage wants you. If they spend it on you and you walk out of it, your team gets a free fight.
Step forward toward your own front line, never toward a side brush.
Tell your team when it's down. For that stretch you're the one who needs peeling.
check: Is Cleanse actually off cooldown, and is your team close enough to turn when they jump you?
breaks: Wrong if their engage is a knock-up or their damage is enough to kill you through it: Cleanse won't save you, so stay back.
basis: pro:Cleanse lets the carry bait the engage

when: an objective spawns within a minute and you have Flash
asks: they keep focusing me before the fight
I get poked out before I can engage
when do I go in as engage support
how do I keep my flash for the fight
say: They'll try to burn your Flash first, so stay behind your tank until it starts, or engage right away if theirs is already gone.
more: A good team removes the engage before the fight. No Flash on you means no fight on your terms.
Hide in a brush your team controls and show only when you're going in.
If they've used their own Flashes poking, that's the signal to start.
check: Which of their Flashes have you seen used, and is your own up?
breaks: Wrong if your team is the one ahead and waiting: you don't need the perfect angle, a plain engage wins.
basis: pro:The engage support is the first target

when: you have Teleport and a dragon, Herald or Baron spawned in the last minute
asks: where do I teleport for the fight
should I TP behind them
do I flank with teleport
I TP'd in and died instantly
say: Teleport to a ward behind your own team and walk in, or flank only if their crowd control has already been used.
more: You can't move while arriving. A team that sees the Teleport will line up every stun on that spot.
Arriving behind your own team costs a couple of seconds and keeps you alive for the whole fight.
The flank is worth it once the fight has started and their abilities are on someone else.
check: Is the ward you're aiming at in a spot they can see, and has the fight started?
breaks: Wrong if their carries are alone and the ward is unseen behind them: that flank ends the fight, take it.
basis: pro:Do not Teleport into their crowd control

asks: they're coming at me from both sides
I'm getting pincered
two of them are flanking me
which way do I run
say: When they come from two sides, hit the weaker side with everything and go through it, or leave before the second group arrives.
more: Standing in the middle means taking both groups at once. One side is always fewer or lower.
Break that side and their far group has to walk through your abilities to reach you.
It only works if you decide early. Half a second of doubt and both arrive together.
check: Which side has fewer or lower enemies, and is your team near either of them?
breaks: Wrong if both sides are healthy and your team is far: don't fight, use Flash toward your nearest tower.
basis: pro:Break a pincer on one side

asks: where do I stand next to my adc
they keep killing both carries
one ult hits me and the adc
should I stand with my other carry
say: Don't stand beside your other carry; spread so one engage can't catch both, or stack only with your tank in front.
more: A two-carry team loses the moment both are caught by the same ability. They know it and aim for it.
If they catch one, the other is free to deal damage and that's often enough to win.
Stay close enough to hit the same target, far enough that one circle can't cover you both.
check: Where is your other damage dealer standing, and where is their engage?
breaks: Wrong if they have assassins rather than area engage: then stand close so you can protect each other.
basis: pro:Two carries, two positions

asks: I can't reach their backline
who do I ult in fights
their carries are too far back
do I flash in for their adc
say: If you can't reach their carries, use everything on whoever dives your team, or step up only once their engage is spent.
more: The diver has left his team to come to you, so he's the one target your whole team can hit.
Kill the front line and their carries have to walk forward into your range.
Flashing forward for the back line usually trades you for nothing.
check: Who is in range right now, and have their engage abilities been used?
breaks: Wrong if their carry has stepped up with no Flash: turn onto him, that ends the fight faster.
basis: pro:Kill the front line you can reach

asks: their top laner keeps diving my adc
should I flank or stay with my carry
who do I go on in fights
their flanker kills my backline every time
say: Shadow their diver and hit him the moment he goes in, or take the flank yourself if he's showing on the other side.
more: One diver kept out of the fight is often the whole fight. Their plan needs him on your carry.
Stand between him and your back line. He has to use his way in on you or not go at all.
It's less exciting than diving, and it's the job when your carry is the one ahead.
check: Where is their diver, and which of your carries is he looking at?
breaks: Wrong if your carries are behind and you're the fed one: then you dive and they follow your lead.
basis: pro:Mark the flanker

asks: we poked them down, do we go in
should I follow up after poke
when do we engage with a poke comp
they're half health, do I dive
say: Once the poke lands, keep poking and make them come to you, or all go together if a carry is nearly dead.
more: Your team is built to win from range. Jumping in swaps that for a fight their team is built for.
A poked team has to leave or engage badly. Either one gives you the objective.
If someone on your team goes in alone, the rest are stuck choosing between following and watching.
check: Who on their team is low, and has anyone on yours already gone in?
breaks: Wrong if they are starting the objective and it's nearly dead: you have to step in to contest, poke won't stop a Smite.
basis: pro:A poke comp does not chase its own poke

when: you have more levels and items than your lane opponent but your carries do not
asks: I'm fed but we're still losing
how do I carry as a tank
I'm ahead but can't kill anyone
what do I do with my lead
say: Your lead only pays as a start, so go on their carry before the next objective, or shove a side lane to pull two.
more: A setup champion ahead doesn't win fights by damage. It wins them by starting on the right target first.
Catch one carry just before a spawn and your team takes the objective without a real fight.
If no angle exists, the side lane makes them answer with two and your team plays four against three.
check: Does their carry have Flash, and is your team close enough to follow you?
breaks: Wrong if your own carries are dead or in base: starting a fight alone just gives your shutdown away.
basis: pro:A fed setup champion must start the fight

when: you have more kills than their carry but only one finished item
asks: I'm fed, can I just fight
I have three kills, do I go in
should I play aggressive now
I'm ahead as adc
say: Kills aren't items yet, so fight from the back as if it's even until the second item, or go in only with your support.
more: With one item you still die to one engage. A shutdown on you gives the lead straight back.
The second item is where an ahead carry starts winning fights alone.
Until then the lead buys you safe farm and first move to objectives, which is plenty.
check: How far are you from the second item, and where is their engage?
breaks: Wrong if their whole team is low after a fight: step up and clean it, that's what the lead is for.
basis: pro:One item is not a carry yet

when: your bot lane has two or more kills before 6:00
asks: we're smashing bot, what now
we got two kills bot, do we push
how do we snowball bot lane
should we take tower or dragon
say: Shove the wave in and take the first dragon with your jungler while they're stuck under tower, or hold the wave if he's top.
more: An early bot lead is worth the most as a dragon, because nobody on their side can walk into the river.
It also gets your jungler ahead, and he pays it back with the next gank.
Holding the wave instead denies them farm. That's the better choice when no jungler is coming.
check: Has your jungler pinged the dragon, and are both enemy laners under their tower?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler and mid are both missing: don't walk into the river, stay with the wave.
basis: pro:Turn an early bot lead into the first dragon

when: four or five enemies died in the last 20 seconds and it is before 20:00
asks: we aced them, what do we take
everyone's dead, baron isn't up
we won the fight, now what
do we push or take dragon
say: Baron isn't up, so take towers and their jungle, recall, and ward the pit before 20:00, or take dragon first if it's alive.
more: With no Baron to take, an ace is paid in towers and in being set up first for the spawn.
A team that respawns into a warded pit and an enemy with fresh items usually gives the Baron too.
Don't dive their base for more kills. The timers are short this early.
check: Is a dragon alive, which tower is closest to falling, and how much gold are you carrying?
breaks: Wrong if their timers are nearly up and you're low: recall first, the towers aren't worth dying for.
basis: pro:An ace before Baron spawns

when: four or five enemies died in the last 20 seconds with different respawn timers
asks: we wiped them, can we end
they're all dead, what do we do
do we take baron or push
aced them late, what now
say: They come back one at a time, so take Baron or an inhibitor now, or recall and buy if your team is low.
more: A wipe that happened over a long chase means staggered respawns. They can't defend as five for a while.
Each one who walks out alone can be killed again, which stretches your time.
Pick the biggest thing the timers allow and commit to it.
check: What are the longest and shortest respawn timers, and how healthy is your team?
breaks: Wrong if their wave-clear champion respawns first and your minions are far: take Baron, not the base.
basis: pro:A staggered wipe comes back in pieces

when: your team killed Baron in the last minute and a dragon spawns within two minutes
asks: we got baron, which lane do we push
where do we go with baron buff
baron then dragon, how do we do both
do we siege mid or bot
say: Push the lane beside the dragon first so the buff and the spawn line up, or siege mid if the dragon's still far off.
more: A buffed wave in the bottom lane pins them there, and you turn to the dragon with them stuck under tower.
Buff and dragon ending together means one push gets both a tower and the stack.
Sieging the far side first leaves you walking across the map as the buff runs out.
check: How long until the dragon, and which lane has your minions closest to their tower?
breaks: Wrong if an inhibitor tower on the other side is nearly dead: finish that, it's worth more than one dragon.
basis: pro:Line the Baron buff up with the dragon

when: your team killed Baron in the last two minutes
asks: there's a wave pushing into our base
who catches the side wave
do I leave the siege to clear top
we have baron but our top is getting pushed
say: Someone has to catch the wave pushing into you; go if you have Teleport or wave clear, or stay if you're the engage.
more: Five in one lane with Baron feels strong, but a wave eating your tower on the far side cancels what you gain.
One player leaving for a few seconds costs the siege nothing. The buffed minions keep them busy.
It also gives that player gold and levels for the fight that follows.
check: Which lane is pushing against you, and who on your team can clear it and get back fastest?
breaks: Wrong if they're about to engage and you're the main damage: stay, lose the wave and win the fight.
basis: pro:A Baron siege still needs the far wave caught

when: your team killed Baron in the last two minutes and an enemy wave-clear champion is alive
asks: we can't break their base with baron
they just clear every wave
how do we siege into wave clear
baron isn't doing anything
say: Against heavy wave clear, push two lanes at once so one wave gets through, or look for a pick on the clearer first.
more: One champion can erase a buffed wave in one lane. He can't stand in two lanes at the same time.
Put your strongest duelist in the second lane, so answering him takes more than one player.
If he steps forward to clear, that's your pick, and then the base is open.
check: Which enemy is clearing the waves, and who on your team can hold a lane alone?
breaks: Wrong if your team is squishy and they have hard engage: splitting gets someone caught, so stay as five and take the outer ring.
basis: pro:Split the Baron push against wave clear

when: the enemy killed Baron in the last two minutes
asks: they have baron, how do we hold
how do I defend the base
do I fight them at the tower
they're sieging with baron
say: Your job is staying alive and killing waves from range, or moving to the second lane if two waves arrive together.
more: A Baron push needs its minions. While you keep deleting them, they can't walk onto your towers.
They want you to step out for a trade. If the wave-clearer dies, the base goes with him.
The buff runs out. Every wave cleared gets you closer to an even game again.
check: Which lane has the bigger wave coming, and where is their engage standing?
breaks: Wrong if they've walked past the minions to dive: then your team fights under the tower together.
basis: pro:The wave-clearer cannot die during Baron

when: the enemy has four dragons or killed Baron in the last two minutes, and Elder has not spawned
asks: they have soul, is it over
how do we come back from this
what do we play for now
do we just defend
say: Defend inhibitors as five and clear waves until Elder, or give a tower if holding it means fighting outside your base.
more: After soul, the next dragon is Elder. That one fight can undo their lead, so the plan is reaching it with a base.
Fights under your towers are the only ones close to even right now.
Use the quiet time to finish items. This late the item gap closes quickly.
check: How long until Elder, and are all three inhibitors still standing?
breaks: Wrong if they leave someone alone in a side lane: take that pick, it's the opening you were waiting for.
basis: pro:Hold the base for the Elder fight

when: after 35:00
asks: what matters this late
it's forty minutes, what do we do
how do we not throw this
everyone's full build, now what
say: This late one death can end it, so move as five to the next Elder or Baron, or stay home clearing if you can't go together.
more: Respawn timers are long enough now that a single pick gives the other team the objective and the base.
Gold barely matters at full build. Position and who sees whom first decide it.
If you're out of wards, recall and buy more instead of walking into the dark.
check: Where is your team, how long until the next big objective, and do you have wards?
breaks: Wrong if you can see all five of them on one side: the lane on the other side is free to push.
basis: pro:Very late, one pick ends the game

when: after 25:00, your team got two or more kills in the last 20 seconds and at least two enemies are alive
asks: can we end
do we go for nexus
should we finish or back off
we killed three, do we end
say: End only if their wave-clearer is dead and your minions are with you; otherwise take Baron and come back with it.
more: Without minions the towers shoot you. A single defender who clears waves can stall until the others respawn.
A failed end leaves you low, far from home and facing five. That's how won games turn.
Baron after a won fight is free, and the next push is the one that finishes.
check: Who is alive on their team, how long are the timers, and is a wave arriving with you?
breaks: Wrong if four are dead with long timers and a big wave is at their base: go, that's the game.
basis: pro:Ending needs minions and a dead defender

when: after 20:00, Baron is alive, you have Teleport and enough gold for an item
asks: do I back before baron
I have gold but baron's up
should I buy or stay with the team
can I recall and TP back
say: Recall and buy right now, then Teleport in when it starts, or stay if your team is already hitting it.
more: An item sitting in your pocket as gold is a fight played at a disadvantage. Teleport lets you fix that for free.
Go early. A Baron can die faster than you expect, and arriving halfway through is worse than not buying.
Tell your team you're in base so they don't start without you.
check: Is anyone hitting Baron yet, and is there a safe ward to Teleport to?
breaks: Wrong if Teleport is down: stay with the team and buy after the fight.
basis: pro:Buy before the Baron fight, not during it

when: after 20:00, Baron is alive and you have Teleport
asks: should I catch the side wave or stay for baron
there's a big wave bot, do I get it
my team's at baron, do I leave
can I go farm bot
say: With Teleport up, go catch the side wave and port back if Baron starts, or stay grouped if it's down.
more: Waiting at the pit for something that might happen costs you the wave, the level and the item you need for the fight.
Teleport means you can be in two places. Use it before the fight, so you arrive stronger.
The wave you push also drags one of them away from the pit.
check: Is there a ward near Baron to Teleport to, and how many enemies are showing?
breaks: Wrong if four enemies are missing and nobody's seen the pit: they may be on it already, so stay.
basis: pro:Teleport lets you leave the group

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: two of them came to stop my split
how do I split as Mordekaiser
they're ganking me in side lane
can I fight two as Morde
say: Keep pushing, and if two come, pull one into Realm of Death for a one-on-one, or back off early if three show.
more: Realm of Death removes the second player for the duel. A two-on-one becomes a fight you can win.
Even if the other one kills you after, you've traded one for one and held two of them far from the objective.
Pick the squishier one. The stats you steal make it shorter.
check: Which of the two can you kill fastest, and can your team take something while they're with you?
breaks: Wrong if the one you'd pull is their fed duelist: he wins inside too, so leave before they reach you.
basis: pro:The split pusher who can isolate one

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: who do I ult as Mordekaiser
should I ult their adc
I ulted and lost the one-on-one
who do I take to the death realm
say: Take a carry you can beat alone into Realm of Death, or pull their engager off your back line if nobody's reachable.
more: Inside it's a pure duel. Pulling in someone who beats you one-on-one just removes you from the fight.
A fed marksman built to kite is often the worst choice, even though he's the one you want dead.
Taking their diver away for a few seconds can be worth more than a kill, because your carries get to shoot freely.
check: Who is ahead on their team, and which of them can't kite or out-duel you?
breaks: Wrong if their carry is low or has no escape left: take him, the duel is already won.
basis: pro:Do not isolate yourself with their strongest duelist

when: you have two finished items
asks: when do I start fights as Vi
who do I ult as Vi
should I wait for my team to engage
how do I play Vi in fights
say: From two items you start the fights: Cease and Desist their carry when your team's in reach, or whoever's alone if they group.
more: It can't be dodged by walking away. A team with you on it chooses when every fight begins.
That only pays if someone follows. Check where your damage is before you go.
Teams without a reliable engage have to wait for mistakes. You don't, so don't play their slower game.
check: Is your team close enough to follow, and who on their side is standing apart?
breaks: Wrong if you're behind and their carry has a protector next to him: take the lone target or wait for the objective.
basis: pro:Reliable engage sets the pace

when: you are level 6
asks: who do I gank at six as Jarvan
is it worth ulting someone with flash
which lane do I go to with ult
I have ult, where do I go
say: At 6, go for whoever has no Flash; Cataclysm traps them for the kill, or use it to force Flash and return.
more: Cataclysm makes an arena around the target. Without Flash, most laners can't leave it.
With Flash up they pay it to get out, and that's still a win: the next visit is the kill.
Go to the lane whose own champion can add damage inside the ring.
check: Which enemy laners have used Flash recently, and is that wave far enough from their tower?
breaks: Wrong if the target has a dash or blink to cross the wall: pick a lane with an immobile champion.
basis: pro:The arena punishes a missing Flash

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: when do I use Bard ult
who do I ult as Bard
I ulted my own team
should I ult the tower
say: Use Tempered Fate to freeze their dive or stop a chaser, or hold it while your own team is mid-combo on the target.
more: It puts everyone it hits into stasis, allies and towers included. A bad one saves the enemy from your team.
Its best uses are defensive: freeze the divers, or make a carry burn Flash so the next play is easy.
On offense, throw it where they're about to be, away from where your team is already hitting.
check: Is your team already hitting that target, and is your own tower inside the circle?
breaks: Wrong if a tower is the only thing keeping your laner alive: freezing it finishes the dive for them.
basis: pro:Stasis hits both sides

asks: they're about to dive me as Gnar
how do I survive a dive on Gnar
when do I use Gnar ult
three of them are top
say: If you're near Mega, wait until they commit under tower and throw them into the wall with GNAR!, or hop away early.
more: GNAR! stuns anyone who hits a wall, and the space behind a tower is full of walls. A dive is the best place to land it.
If your jungler is near, that stun turns their dive into your double kill.
As small Gnar you have none of that, so judge your Rage before deciding to stay.
check: How close are you to transforming, and is your jungler on your side of the map?
breaks: Wrong if you're low on Rage: you'll stay small and die, so leave the wave and go.
basis: pro:The dived laner who holds his ultimate

when: you got a kill in the last minute
asks: I just cashed in, what now
I got a kill as Draven, do I back
what do I do with all this gold
should I keep fighting
say: Recall and turn the cash-out into a finished item, then force the next objective, or stay for plates if it's two minutes off.
more: League of Draven pays extra gold on a kill. It's worth nothing until it becomes an item.
A finished item several minutes early is the point where the other team can't walk up to a dragon.
Staying to fight again with the gold in your pocket risks a shutdown that hands it all back.
check: How much gold are you holding, and when does the next objective spawn?
breaks: Wrong if both of them are dead and the tower is nearly down: take the tower first, then recall.
basis: pro:Cash in, buy, then force

when: you are below level 6
asks: I'm losing lane as Kassadin
how do I play early as Kass
I can't farm in this lane
when do I get strong
say: Early your job is to lose slowly: take the farm that's safe and the levels, or roam with your jungler if the lane's frozen.
more: You're weak before Riftwalk and get stronger with each rank of it. Minions you miss now matter less than deaths.
The other team knows that and will stack dragons to force fights before you're ready.
So count their dragons. You can give the early ones, but not the one that gives them soul.
check: How many dragons do they have, and where is their jungler while you're pushed in?
breaks: Wrong if their mid laner roams every wave: follow or shove, because their lead on the map hurts more than your lane.
basis: pro:The scaling pick loses lane gracefully
